NSSCO Examiners Report 2020
GEOGRAPHY
6137
Paper 1
GENERAL COMMENTS
1 Many candidates do not follow instructions.
2 Many candidates struggled with comparison questions.  Teach candidates how to answer these 
questions in class.
3 Selective teaching took place.  Please make sure that you teach and that candidates study the complete 
syllabus, not just sections of it.
4 Candidates do not read complete questions.  They only read sections of the questions, and can 
therefore not score marks in these questions.
5 There is a difference between: state, describe, explain, suggest, etc.  Make sure candidates know how to 
answer each of these command words.
6 It is very important for candidates to know that when answers are numbered, only one answer 
per number is allowed.  Markers will only mark the first answer if there are more than one.  The 
markers will not choose for the candidate.  Every number must have only one answer.
7 Only when no numbers are indicated, can candidates write more than one answer on a line.
8 If and when the question requires an example to be given with the answer candidates must do 
so.  If no example is given, no mark can be awarded.
COMMENTS ON SPECIFIC QUESTIONS
1 (a) (i) Answered fairly well.  Some candidates could not give the correct definition, while some only 
gave examples.
Expected answers:
Natural phenomena which cause harm/a dangerous event resulting from the Earth’s forces
 (ii) Well answered.  Most candidates could give the correct examples.
Expected answers:
A = Earthquake/volcanic eruption
B = Drought/tropical storm/flood
 (iii) Fairly answered.  Many candidates struggled to make the comparisons.  Many only lifted the 
data without making the comparisons.
Expected answers:
Droughts are more predictable/earthquakes unpredictable
Droughts affect bigger areas/earthquakes affect smaller areas
Earthquakes have more short-term affects
Droughts have more long-term affects
 (iv) Answered fairly well.  Candidates listed the answers.  Many did not differentiate between LEDCs 
and MEDCs; they wrote in general and lost marks.
Expected answers:
Quality of buildings
Prediction/preparedness/warning systems
Evacuation procedures
Education re precautions
Drills
Level of medical care/emergency services
Rescue procedures
Accessibility for rescue/infrastructure development

practice-based sources to enhance their teaching.

candidates will soon develop the skills to analyse data from tables, graphs and diagrams sufficiently to meet the
